questions.prompt: Tell me about one thing you ate yesterday. Say it in two short sentences, like "I had an apple." or "I ate an egg."
questions.context: Daily life — talking about food you had

questions.prompt: What do you want to buy this week? Tell me two or three short sentences about small things — an umbrella, an eraser, an ice cream.
Tell me about one hour of your evening. Use short sentences like "I watched TV for an hour." What did you do for an hour last night?
questions.context: Daily life — evening routine and time

questions.prompt: Tell me about someone in your family or your team. Say what their job is in a short sentence, for example "He is an engineer." or "She is an office worker."
questions.context: Light work talk — introducing a person and their job

questions.prompt: You need to write down your work plan for tomorrow. Tell me in two short sentences what you want to make — an email, an action plan, an idea list.
questions.context: Light work talk — planning tomorrow's small tasks

instruction.hint_timing: wait about five seconds, then give a short hint; correct the missing or mispronounced 'an' right after the learner finishes speaking

level.reason: 짧은 단문은 편하게 말하지만 관사와 'an' 발음이 아직 불안정해서 A2에서 더 다져야 해요.

notes: Articles appear when the learner repeats a memorized chunk ("a meeting", "a report") but disappear with new nouns like "joke", "action plan", "project architecture meeting".
Speaks in fragments and then joins them; the article is most often lost in the second fragment.
'an' is reduced to 'a' in speech even when the written form is correct — needs slow syllable-level repetition.
Longer answers trigger past-tense slips ("yesterday i go"), so keep sentences short for now.
